facts.statement: Sinornithomimus lived during the Late Cretaceous, possibly younger than approximately 92 million years ago.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, ?(younger than ~92 Ma)

facts.statement: Sinornithomimus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 92 million years ago during the Turonian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 92 millones de años durante el Turoniense

facts.statement: The fossils of Sinornithomimus were found in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Asia

facts.statement: The first remains of Sinornithomimus were found in 1997 and formally described in 2003.
facts.quote: The first remains were found in 1997 and described six years later in 2003 as the new genus and species Sinornithomimus dongi.

facts.statement: Dong Zhiming uncovered the first Sinornithomimus fossils in 1997 as part of the Mongol Highland International Dinosaur Project.
facts.quote: The first fossil remains of Sinornithomimus were uncovered by Dong Zhiming in the Ulansuhai Formation as part of the Mongol Highland International Dinosaur Project in 1997.

facts.statement: The initial discovery included at least fourteen skeletons, with nine being nearly complete and uncrushed.
facts.quote: They contained at least fourteen skeletons found in close association, nine of which are nearly complete and relatively uncrushed.

facts.statement: The pristine condition of the bones suggests a catastrophic event killed all individuals in the find simultaneously and instantly.
facts.quote: The unweathered state of the bones, preserved in siltstone interspersed with layers of clay and the absence of evidence for post-mortem movement, argue for a catastrophic event that killed all the individuals present in the find simultaneously and instantaneously.

facts.statement: Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Lü Junchang named and described the type species Sinornithomimus dongi in 2003.
facts.quote: The type species Sinornithomimus dongi was named and described by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Lü Junchang in 2003.

facts.statement: A 2001 expedition found another herd of thirteen juveniles and subadults at the same site.
facts.quote: A second expedition in 2001 at the same site led to the discovery of another fossilized herd of thirteen juveniles and subadults of Sinornithomimus.

facts.statement: The high number of nearly intact specimens makes Sinornithomimus the most completely known ornithomimid.
facts.quote: The second discovery also largely consisted of nearly intact exemplars making Sinornithomimus the most completely known ornithomimid.

facts.statement: Sinornithomimus was a small ornithomimid measuring 2.5 meters in length and weighing about 91 kilograms.
facts.quote: Sinornithomimus was a small ornithomimid measuring 2.5 m in length and weighing about 91 kg with a relatively short neck and head for a member of that group.

facts.statement: Gastroliths found in the stomach areas of fossil skeletons support the hypothesis that Sinornithomimus was a herbivore.
facts.quote: The herbivory of this genus is supported by the rare presence of gastroliths, as such stones were found forming conspicuous masses in the stomach areas of the fossil skeletons.

facts.statement: Fossil arrangements in bonebeds with similarly aged juveniles corroborate that this species was gregarious.
facts.quote: This species was gregarious, which is corroborated by the arrangement of the fossil remains in a small bonebed with the juvenile individuals being approximately of the same age.

facts.statement: While originally assumed to form familial protective groups, a 2008 study suggests juvenile herds were left to fend for themselves while adults nested or brooded.
facts.quote: It was assumed by the describers that adults protected themselves and their juveniles from predators by forming familial groups; in 2008 however a study concluded that the all juvenile herds suggest that immature individuals were left to fend for themselves in juvenile groups while adults preoccupied themselves with nesting or brooding.

facts.statement: It is believed to have been a herbivore, supported by the presence of gastroliths found as visible masses in the stomach areas of fossil skeletons.
facts.quote: Se cree que fue un herbívoro apoyado por la presencia gastrolitos, pues tales piedras fueron encontradas como masas visibles en las áreas del estómago de los esqueletos fósiles.

facts.statement: This species was gregarious, corroborated by the arrangement of fossils in a small bonebed of juvenile individuals of nearly the same age.
facts.quote: Esta especie era gregaria, algo corroborado por la disposición de los fósiles que se encuentran en un pequeño lecho de huesos de los individuos juveniles que están casi en la misma edad.

facts.statement: The increase in running ability with growth is supported by adults having relatively longer lower legs, indicating cursorial proportions.
facts.quote: Esto además está apoyado por el aumento de la capacidad corredora del animal que progresaba en su crecimiento, siendo las proporciones de los adultos más propias del tipo corredor, poseyendo la parte inferior de las piernas relativamente más largas.

facts.statement: A 2001 expedition discovered a herd of juvenile Sinornithomimus fossils in the Gobi Desert in western Inner Mongolia.
facts.quote: Una expedición de 2001 llevó al descubrimiento de una manada de jóvenes Sinornithomimus fosilizados, en el desierto de Gobi en la Mongolia Interior occidental.

facts.statement: A 2008 study argues that the juvenile herd suggests immature individuals were left to protect themselves after adults protected them in the nest.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2008, argumenta que la manada juvenil sugiere que dejaban a los individuos no maduros para protegerse por sí mismos después de que los adultos los protegieran en el nido.

facts.statement: Originally assigned to Ornithomimidae, Sinornithomimus was considered a basal ornithomimid more derived than Archaeornithomimus, though recent analyses reverse this relationship.
facts.quote: Sinornithomimus was by the describers assigned to the Ornithomimidae. It was a basal ornithomimid that was considered by its describers a more derived form than Archaeornithomimus, though more recent analyses reverse the situation.

facts.statement: Sinornithomimus belongs to the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: familia: Ornithomimidae

facts.statement: The genus of this dinosaur is Sinornithomimus.
facts.quote: genus: Sinornithomimus

facts.statement: The only known species is S. dongi.
facts.quote: species: S. dongi

facts.statement: It is debated whether adults formed familial protective groups or if juvenile herds were left to fend for themselves while adults nested or brooded.
facts.quote: It was assumed by the describers that adults protected themselves and their juveniles from predators by forming familial groups; in 2008 however a study concluded that the all juvenile herds suggest that immature individuals were left to fend for themselves in juvenile groups while adults preoccupied themselves with nesting or brooding.

facts.statement: Sinornithomimus is classified as a basal ornithomimid.
facts.quote: Sinornithomimus es un ornitomímido basal

facts.statement: The animal possesses some plesiomorphic synapomorphies of ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Sinornithomimus posee algunas sinapomorfias plesiomorficas de los ornitomímidos

facts.statement: The parent group of Sinornithomimus is the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ornithomimidae

facts.statement: Sinornithomimus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Sinornithomimus lived during the Turonian stage, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Sinornithomimus was named by Kobayashi and Lü in 2003.
facts.quote: Kobayashi and Lü 2003

facts.statement: It was initially considered more derived than Archaeornithomimus, but later analyses reversed this view.
facts.quote: fue considerado por los autores como más derivado que el Archaeornithomimus, pero análisis posteriores revirtieron esta visión

facts.statement: The hand structure of Sinornithomimus is similar to Archaeornithomimus, representing an intermediate position between the ornithomimosaur Harpymimus and more advanced ornithomimids.
facts.quote: La estructura de la mano es similar a la de Archaeornithomimus representando una posición intermedia entere el ornitomimosauriano Harpymimus y los más avanzados ornitomímidos

facts.statement: The distinction between Asian and North American ornithomimids is based on the maxilla being covered in vascular foramina found in the latter.
facts.quote: basados en el maxilar cubiertos de foramnenes vasculares encontrado en estos últimos

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Sinornithomimus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
